prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1470; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck stiffness at the scene and was transported to urgent care by ambulance. Police report requested. Liability appears clear pending photos and driver statements.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirms wrist pain on the left side and was told at urgent care that imaging showed a fracture. Claimant has not retained an attorney and says they are handling the matter directly. Explained the claims process, the need for medical records, and the option to seek independent advice if they wish. Requested authorization to obtain treatment records.

Entry 3: Received the police report. It notes the at-fault driver admitted to looking at a phone before impact. Witness statement from a bystander corroborates that the rear vehicle did not brake. Photos of both vehicles show rear bumper damage on the claimant vehicle consistent with a moderate-speed impact. Liability assessment updated to reflect the at-fault driver as primary.

Entry 4: Claimant forwarded orthopedic consultation notes. Diagnosis is a closed fracture of the distal radius, treated with a splint and referral for possible surgical consult. Claimant reports difficulty with daily tasks, including driving and typing. Advised claimant that a rental vehicle is available under the policy's rental provision if needed. Claimant said they would think about it and follow up.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Claimant states the surgical consult is scheduled and asked how the bodily injury portion of the claim is evaluated. Explained that the adjuster will review medical records and bills once treatment concludes, and that a settlement cannot be finalized until the treatment course is known. Claimant agreed to send wage loss documentation. File remains open, reserves under review.
